correctness.rationale: The Fourier basis is complete for C3×CN. Branch eigenvalues have multiplicities 1 or 2 in the first factor and 1 or 2 in the odd second factor; within each branch all cosine levels are distinct. Every positive cross-branch collision is exactly gamma=3/(mu_t-mu_s), t<s. A t=0 collision has eigenspace dimension four and t>=1 has dimension six; simultaneous equal-parameter collisions cannot merge more than one level per branch. Eigenspace dimension gives the universal sensor lower bound. The four-site restriction is invertible on all four-dimensional blocks, including the mixed collision, via a nonzero 2-by-2 determinant (z-1)(z^-1-1)(z^-1-z). Six sites resolve the full C3 Fourier block and the two y frequencies independently, even at six-dimensional collisions. The time Vandermonde at at most N+1 eigenvalues proves finite-time recovery. The saved checker replayed 1020 sampled cases and 28210 finite assertions; the analytical proof supplies infinite-N validity.
